official_resources.title: 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight
official_resources.key_takeaway: Maps the five interconnected hazards of deep-space travel: Space Radiation, Isolation and Confinement, Distance from Earth, Gravity Fields, and Hostile Closed Environments.

official_resources.title: Risks of Human Spaceflight
official_resources.key_takeaway: Catalogs specific clinical risks including SANS, Altered Immune System Responses (latent virus reactivation & rashes), Cardiovascular Adaptation, Bone Changes, Host-Microorganism Interactions, and Inadequate Sleep.

official_resources.title: Ongoing HRP Research in Space
official_resources.key_takeaway: Covers Artemis II Standard Measures (activity, sleep, blood/saliva immune biomarkers), SANS thigh-cuff & B-vitamin mitigation trials, spinal scans for bone/muscle loss, and commercial telemedicine testing.

official_resources.title: Monitoring Radiation for Astronaut Health
official_resources.key_takeaway: Highlights Canadian active radiation dosimetry (CANS neutron spectrometer, EVARM, MOSFET, Radi-N) to track cosmic and solar particle radiation exposure on Artemis/Moon/Mars missions.

official_resources.title: Why Do We Conduct Science Experiments in Space?
official_resources.key_takeaway: Explains how microgravity accelerates bone density loss, muscle atrophy, and cardiovascular changes aboard ISS, driving both crew countermeasures and Earth remote-health innovations.

spacecraft.label: Spacecraft Transit
spacecraft.description: Deep-space transit vehicle with elevated cosmic/solar radiation, 0g cephalad fluid shift, and significant communication latency.

station.label: Space Station (ISS / Gateway)
station.description: Orbital habitat with near-real-time ground contact, musculoskeletal unloading, and closed-loop CO2 scrubbing.

rover.label: Lunar / Mars Rover (EVA)
rover.description: Pressurized rover or EVA sortie with elevated cardiovascular workload, suit thermal rise, and unshielded solar radiation risk.

base.label: Planetary Base
base.description: Long-duration surface base with partial gravity, lunar/Martian regolith dust irritation risk, and prolonged isolation.

body_zones.label: Heart & Vessels
body_zones.reference_title: NASA HRP — Risks of Human Spaceflight
body_zones.organ_function: Maintains systemic perfusion and blood pressure regulation under altered gravity.
body_zones.default_summary: Resting HR and BP within microgravity baseline.
body_zones.space_hazard: Gravity Fields (cephalad fluid shift) & Hostile Closed Environments (CO2 load)
body_zones.why_exam_needed: Weightlessness alters blood circulation and how the heart and blood vessels function, shrinking plasma volume and increasing cardiovascular adaptation risk.
body_zones.self_exam_guide: Sit still for 3 minutes, wrap cuff at heart level, press Measure, and log systolic/diastolic values per Artemis II Standard Measures.

body_zones.label: Lungs / Airway
body_zones.hrp_risk_name: Risk of Host-Microorganism Interactions & Closed-Habitat CO2
body_zones.reference_title: NASA HRP — 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight
body_zones.organ_function: Gas exchange (O2 intake and CO2 clearance) inside pressurized spacecraft/habitat atmosphere.
body_zones.default_summary: Airway and cabin CO2 response remain stable.
body_zones.space_hazard: Hostile Closed Environments (CO2 scrubber drift, airborne particulates, hypoxia risk during EVA pre-breathe)
body_zones.why_exam_needed: Elevated cabin CO2 or pulmonary fluid shift inside a closed spacecraft ecosystem can trigger headaches, tachypnea, and B-line artifacts on lung ultrasound.
body_zones.self_exam_guide: Check cabin CO2 readout, perform a 4-zone anterior chest ultrasound sweep if short of breath, and log resting HR.

body_zones.label: Bones & Spine
body_zones.reference_title: CSA — Why Do We Conduct Science Experiments in Space?
body_zones.organ_function: Structural support, calcium homeostasis, and intervertebral spacing.
body_zones.default_summary: ARED resistive countermeasures on track with no acute metabolic strain.
body_zones.space_hazard: Gravity Fields (bone mineral density loss and spinal muscle unloading in 0g)
body_zones.why_exam_needed: Without gravity, bones break down faster (1-1.5% BMD loss/month); NASA HRP scrutinizes spinal scans and non-treadmill resistive exercises to prevent brittle bone fractures.
body_zones.self_exam_guide: Complete daily 30-min ARED resistive routine, log lower-back stiffness, and maintain morning glucose checks.

body_zones.label: Kidneys / Fluid
body_zones.hrp_risk_name: Risk of Inadequate Food and Nutrition & Renal Stone Mobilization
body_zones.reference_title: NASA HRP — Ongoing HRP Research in Space
body_zones.organ_function: Fluid balance, electrolyte filtration, and renal stone risk prevention.
body_zones.default_summary: Hydration and metabolic glucose indicators remain balanced.
body_zones.space_hazard: Gravity Fields (bone calcium mobilization increasing renal stone risk) & Isolation
body_zones.why_exam_needed: Bone resorption releases calcium while reduced thirst cues and altered spaceflight diet/metabolism elevate kidney stone and insulin-resistance risk.
body_zones.self_exam_guide: Track 2.5 L daily fluid intake, log morning blood glucose in mg/dL, and run bladder/kidney ultrasound if flank discomfort occurs.

body_zones.label: Skin
body_zones.hrp_risk_name: Risk of Host-Microorganism Interactions & Viral Reactivation Rashes
body_zones.reference_title: NASA HRP — Risks of Human Spaceflight
body_zones.organ_function: Primary barrier against dry cabin air, altered microbiome, and ionizing radiation.
body_zones.default_summary: No erythema flare or radiation-associated skin irritation flagged.
body_zones.space_hazard: Hostile Closed Environments (skin microbiome shifts) & Space Radiation
body_zones.why_exam_needed: Spaceflight stress can awaken inactive viruses causing rashes, while skin microbiomes shift in closed habitats, increasing dermatitis and infection risk.
body_zones.self_exam_guide: Capture a well-lit close-up photo of any rash or irritation using the Vision Camera in Skin/Eye mode.

body_zones.label: Immune System
body_zones.hrp_risk_name: Risk of Altered Immune System Responses & Radiation Exposure
body_zones.reference_title: CSA — Monitoring Radiation for Astronaut Health
body_zones.organ_function: Cellular defense and inflammation regulation under cosmic/neutron radiation and stress.
body_zones.default_summary: Body temperature and cumulative radiation dose remain within nominal bounds.
body_zones.space_hazard: Space Radiation (CSA CANS/Radi-N neutron & dosimetry tracking) & Isolation Stress
body_zones.why_exam_needed: Artemis II blood/saliva studies show deep-space radiation and flight stress alter immune responses and elevate long-term cancer and infection risk.
body_zones.self_exam_guide: Verify personal CSA radiation dosimeter reading (mSv), measure oral temperature, and log fever, rash, or swollen nodes.

body_zones.label: Brain / Cognition
body_zones.hrp_risk_name: Risk of Inadequate Sleep, Irregular Schedules & Behavioral Changes
body_zones.reference_title: NASA HRP — Ongoing HRP Research in Space
body_zones.organ_function: Executive alertness, circadian synchronization, and emotional resilience.
body_zones.default_summary: Sleep architecture and behavioral mood state are nominal.
body_zones.space_hazard: Isolation and Confinement & Distance from Earth (140M-mile autonomy)
body_zones.why_exam_needed: Chronic sleep loss, shifting work schedules, and prolonged confinement erode cognitive performance, teamwork, and behavioral health.
body_zones.self_exam_guide: Log sleep hours upon waking, rate mood 1-10 honestly (Artemis II Standard Measures), and follow wake-shift light cycles.

body_zones.label: Eyes (SANS)
body_zones.hrp_risk_name: Risk of Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS)
body_zones.reference_title: NASA HRP — Risks of Human Spaceflight
body_zones.organ_function: Ocular acuity, optic nerve head integrity, and intracranial fluid balance.
body_zones.default_summary: No fluid-shift or circadian strain warning affecting ocular health.
body_zones.space_hazard: Gravity Fields (intracranial fluid pressure & SANS) & Closed Air
body_zones.why_exam_needed: Fluid pressure inside the skull during prolonged microgravity can reshape the eyes and optic nerve; HRP researches thigh cuffs and B-vitamin countermeasures.
body_zones.self_exam_guide: Capture an eye close-up photo if redness or visual blur occurs, check blood pressure, and run Amsler grid self-test.
